subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should persisted per-session `/exec` defaults ever be allowed to keep a less restrictive exec policy than current global or agent config after a session resumes?
rationale: Current source and tests make persisted session defaults intentional, but the reported failure mode is security-sensitive because later operator policy changes can be shadowed by old session state.

options.title: Clamp to current config
options.body: Make global or agent exec policy the effective upper bound for stored session defaults, with regression coverage for stricter upgrades.

options.title: Keep persistence as-is
options.body: Document that operators must reset sessions or run a repair flow when changing exec policy for existing Discord lanes.

options.title: Add reset or doctor first
options.body: Ship an explicit operator-facing session exec reset or doctor repair before changing precedence semantics.

recommendation.title: Clamp to current config
recommendation.body: Make global or agent exec policy the effective upper bound for stored session defaults, with regression coverage for stricter upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest history trail for `/exec` session override behavior and tests points to steipete.
